answer: A capacity-bounded trust graph resists Sybil attacks by evaluating max-flow across credit-limited peer edges. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of cultivating authentic bilateral relationships to cross graph cuts, exposing free identity scaling as a fable. Adversary subgraphs cannot drain this transactional oasis and stay trapped in an economic tundra without routing capacity. A major limitation is that legitimate new agents suffer cold-start starvation before securing trusted sponsors.
